scores.notes: The plan uses a restrained portrait of Holmes to convey the paragraph's description of his temperament. No literal meeting with Irene or appearance by narrator Watson is introduced.
The verse states a belief about those who love God; it does not stage Paul delivering a courtyard speech. The selected Paul and his speaking action import the writer into that statement.
The text attributes release from the net to Yahweh, whereas the action makes David stoop to free his own foot. The upward gaze and unfigured radiance otherwise fit the verse's imagery.
The father commands servants to bring a robe, ring and sandals for the younger son, and all these subjects appear in the plan. The parable's father is depicted as its human character.
Daniel speaks to the king while unharmed among quiet lions, matching his testimony and direct address. An angelic glow conveys the intervention without introducing a bodily God.
Peter's coat-wrapped leap and the beloved disciple's recognition are the verse's central action and are both shown. The distant shore figure represents the Lord whom they recognize.
The hypothetical defendant in 'If anyone sues you' becomes Jesus personally surrendering his clothes. The selected disciples are also placed in the invented litigation scene.
Alice, the Hatter, March Hare and sleepy Dormouse all participate in the exchange at the tea table. Their simultaneous reactions can illustrate the conversation without depicting separate events.
The Caterpillar pauses with its hookah and addresses a shy Alice, as in the passage. Mushroom scale and the facing composition preserve the animal encounter.
The statement about believers being in Christ is converted into Paul teaching in a Corinthian house. The verse does not place its writer physically with the addressees.
The soldiers cast lots and divide garments below the crucified Jesus, matching the verse. The partly shadowed crucifixion remains serious and avoids lingering gore.
The first-person flower comparison supports a portrait of the Shulammite with roses and lilies. The meadow is an interpretive setting, but the speaker herself is the comparison's subject.
An unnamed husband moves from his parents toward his wife, illustrating the relationship described in the quotation. No named author or listener is inserted.

Holmes reassures Helen with a hand on her forearm, and Watson is explicitly present in secondaryElements. The glove ticket and muddy sleeve preserve the passage's clues without requesting readable lettering.

The passage culminates in Holmes offering his lens and asking Watson to examine the hat; the plan instead makes Holmes the active examiner. That reverses the narrated handoff under the rule to follow the moment and clues.
Alice is simultaneously mid-leap, toppling the box and stooping to collect jurors, while Bill is already replaced upside down. These are successive stages of the accident and recovery in the text.

The king presses his signet at the stone sealing the den, with court lords nearby. Daniel is enclosed rather than required as a visible figure, and neither a signet nor an unspecified wax tablet necessarily requests writing.
Watson ('I') holds the printed slip to the light in the passage, but the plan assigns that action to Holmes. The printed slip and spread typewritten letters also explicitly request visible writing.

The command to journey through the listed lands becomes Moses physically directing a gathering beneath Horeb. Moses is selected as the speaking actor although this moment's words do not stage him delivering them.

A genealogy heading is turned into an invented scene of a scribe unrolling a scroll before onlookers. The partly unfurled scroll and 'opening lines of text' request writing even with the qualification that it is unreadable.

The horses, chariots and Egyptian pursuers are shown in the sea corridor. The Israelites referred to by 'after them' are not actually described as visible; 'the Israelite side ahead' only gives a direction.
Light spreads across darkness and primordial waters, directly illustrating the creation of light. God's action is represented through radiance without a body or figure.

The plan makes Isaiah the man beneath the seraphim, whereas the verse places them above 'him', the divine subject of the vision. Isaiah is inserted as a visible central observer, while the six-wing arrangement itself follows the text.
Mary and Joseph return to Jerusalem and search among people in the streets, matching the verse's return and search. Jesus is appropriately absent from the unsuccessful search scene.
Daniel's refusal of rewards before the king is accurately staged. However, secondaryElements explicitly substitutes a blank wall for the writing that Daniel promises to read.

John is added as a standing observer although the verse describes the glassy sea and four creatures around the throne. The selected formless God is assigned a central throne from which radiance rises, meeting the rubric's explicit seat-or-throne criterion.
Adam's death is represented by an aged man lying still, with restrained mourning. Adam is named in the verse even though the section cast is empty.
Both named cities receive falling sulfur and fire, the central event of the verse. Divine presence is suggested through light without a bodily figure.

The dancers explicitly say they can do without lobsters, but secondaryElements puts the song's lobsters and turtles on the actual shingle behind Alice. This merges the sung scene with the enacted dance.
Alice struggles with the twisting flamingo among hedgehogs and card-soldier arches while the Queen stamps about. The card soldiers are explicitly flat and the threatened violence remains comic.

The plan depicts the King's hasty notebook closure and the present court figures. It never makes Alice's exceptional size readable against the furniture or other figures, despite the size-focused passage and explicit depiction rule.

The inkstand is still being hurled while it is already spilled and ink is dripping down Bill's face, merging impact and aftermath. The Knave is explicitly added although this excerpt does not place him in the described exchange.
Hezekiah's wholehearted temple service is illustrated through purposeful supervision of work and offerings. This is a concrete rendering of the activity summarized by the verse.
Holmes lashes at the bell-pull in the flare of a match as Watson squints, matching the sudden action. Omitting a visible snake respects Watson's explicit inability to see what Holmes struck.
Saul's sudden illumination near Damascus matches the verse. The selected 'men with Saul' are additionally staged reacting, although this moment's text only places Saul on the road.

The verse evokes the laying of the earth's foundations, but the plan shows Job rising on an ash heap before a whirlwind. It substitutes the listener's reaction for the described creation scene and omits the foundations.

Hatherley points out the bushes and window while Holmes watches, consistent with their conversation. The station-master is additionally identified in secondaryElements although this excerpt only establishes a crowd, Hatherley and Holmes.

The line concerns Obed fathering Jesse and Jesse fathering David; the plan instead returns to Naomi holding infant Obed. Jesse and David are absent, while Naomi and the women are imported into an invented recitation.
Peter steps onto the water toward Jesus as the verse describes. The selected Twelve are also shown leaning over the boat, although the moment's text names only Peter and Jesus as present figures.
Alice speaks guardedly to the Cat while the Queen listens close behind, capturing her interrupted criticism. The floating head and nearby croquet setting preserve the encounter.

The vision says the old heaven and earth have passed and the sea is no more, while the action still depicts a churning sea dissolving. A visible lone seer is also inserted into the landscape he reports seeing.
Alice is made to hold the Cat's head physically, an action absent from their conversation. The Queen also glances over her shoulder despite the text's explicit 'without even looking round'.

Daniel and an attendant assembly are placed visibly inside a verse focused on the Ancient of Days and thrones. The selected formless Ancient of Days is represented at a fiery throne, which the embodied-effects rubric explicitly includes.

Jesus commands the water and the storm settles, matching the central action. The selected Twelve and their detailed reactions are additional recurring figures not placed in this verse's scene by its text.

The filling boat and crashing waves fit the verse. The plan additionally selects and stages the Twelve bailing and rowing, although the moment's text describes the storm and boat without identifying their occupants.

The same spear is gripped by Saul, leaving his hand, and already embedded in the wall, combining successive instants. The haze is explicitly identified as the evil spirit, which this verse does not put in the scene.
The plan chooses the early instant when the Cat's eyes are forming and Alice still holds her flamingo. The later full head and conversation need not be shown in that instant.
An unnamed weary man regaining strength illustrates the weak recipient described by the verse. Isaiah is not inserted, and no divine bodily figure is requested.
Ezekiel addresses the dry bones with an uplifted arm, illustrating the explicitly commanded address. The bones and valley dominate the scene without embodied divinity.

Holmes and Watson observe the pawnbroker's assistant in the correct square. The phrase 'brown board with blank lettering' is internally ambiguous: a blank sign would avoid writing, but visible lettering would trigger visible_writing.
Naomi addresses Ruth and advises her about the fields, so both women belong in the conversation. The plan does not place Naomi among the maidens whose company she recommends.
This verse is Jesus' call, but the plan already shows Lazarus stepping out in grave cloths. It also selects and depicts the recurring crowd, which this moment's text does not identify.
Moses' order, its proclamation and the people's restraint are represented by the herald and people stopping their offerings. These actions can share the same camp scene.

The coffee conversation involves the correct three family members. However, the plan moves the locked bureau into the drawing-room, whereas the passage locates it in Holder's own room and ends with Arthur following him there.
The child, wolf, lamb, leopard, goat, calf and young lion are shown peacefully together. The additional 'fattened calf' explicitly listed in the verse is absent from the plan's animal list.

The inspector questions the station-master as their train departs, but the plan leaves Holmes and Watson at the open door of that receding train. It splits the arriving investigative party between the platform and a departing carriage.
Saul clutches Samuel's robe as it tears during Samuel's turn to leave. The torn cloth and the two named actors preserve the moment.
The disciples wake Jesus from the stern cushion in desperation, exactly the encounter described. The plan captures his stirring rather than advancing to the rebuke of the storm.

The promise concerns mercy and rescue for Judah, but the plan centers Hosea, Gomer and Lo-Ruhamah at home. The prophet and his family replace the promised people; distant hills alone do not depict the house of Judah being saved.
Jonah is enclosed within the great fish, illustrating the stated period in its belly. The interior view does not require a separate exterior fish or bodily divine actor.
Daniel is hauled unharmed from the den while the king reaches toward him, matching the extraction and gladness. Attendants supply the unnamed agents of 'was taken up'.
Rephaiah is explicitly present in primarySubject and supervises repairs to Jerusalem's wall. His omission from the selected cast list does not omit him from the actual scene plan.

The verse contrasts present partial sight with future full knowledge, but the action turns this into an immediate encounter with a companion in a doorway. It collapses 'now' and 'then' into a single ordinary social action.
The general statement about hearing and faith becomes a specific street sermon by Paul. Nothing in the moment places the writer among a listening crowd.

Holmes kneeling with lens and lantern and Merryweather seated on a crate match the passage. Watson, directly addressed as 'Doctor' and participating in the conversation, is absent from all plan fields.
The crowded corner, sleeping Dormouse used as a cushion and Alice's indignant arrival are all preserved. The cry of 'No room!' can reasonably continue as she sits.

The proverb's comparison of heavens, earth and kings' hidden hearts is replaced by Hezekiah's scribes contemplating a scroll. The compilers are inserted as actors, and no king or corresponding central subject is depicted.
The Rabbit unfolds the paper to read its verses, which requests a visible written document. Alice and the Knave remain present in secondaryElements despite their omission from selected.
Elisha climbs toward Bethel while youths come from the gate and mock him. The plan remains at the taunting encounter and preserves his dignity.
Moses, the rock, abundant water, congregation and drinking livestock all appear. Aaron is additionally named as standing nearby, although this verse does not place him in the scene.

Abraham holds the knife over Isaac before striking, matching the threatened sacrifice without gore. Servants are additionally depicted down the slope, though this moment only places Abraham and his son at the action.
The plan chooses the encamped phase with the cloud resting over the tabernacle and families staying put. It need not also depict departure, which would introduce another instant.
Families unload and erect tents after travel, matching the arrival and encampment in Terah. The generic wilderness setting does not substitute a conflicting named destination.

Watson's crouched wait and the first floor glint fit the excerpt, but the lighting is explicitly attributed to a faintly glowing shuttered lantern. The passage emphasizes that Holmes's lantern leaves absolute darkness until a new light appears at the floor.
Jesus turns and looks toward Peter, who realizes the remembered warning; both are explicitly described in the plan. The quoted earlier prediction is not staged as a separate encounter.
Alice timidly asks directions while the Cat grins with visible teeth and claws. The plan keeps the two present speakers together in the wood.
The exiles sit and weep beside Babylon's river while remembering Zion. The remembered city is not incorrectly made their current location.

The verse describes Ammon making war against Israel, but the plan relocates the encounter to Jephthah's outlaw band in Tob. Jephthah is selected and placed at the front although this moment does not introduce him into the war.

Moses seated on the stone with Aaron and Hur supporting his arms matches the verse. Joshua, Israelite fighters and Amalekites are additionally selected and staged in a battle below, which the moment's text does not depict.
The direct accusation 'You have done foolishly' supports depicting the seer's rebuke of Asa. The plan preserves that confrontation without literal eyes or a bodily Yahweh.

The Hatter bites his teacup under the Queen's stare, with the named companions and jury present. The recurring court officers are also explicitly added at attention although this excerpt does not place them in the action.

The plan includes the shouting Israelites, priests with trumpets, falling wall and entry into Jericho. A breach can open while adjacent masonry is still falling, so the action need not require separate instants.
Alice's very long neck winds through the treetops toward the accusing Pigeon and its eggs. The visual scale and animal depiction follow the passage and rules.
The masked visitor pauses at the door with his hand at the vizard while Holmes and Watson watch. The disguise, rich dress and arriving carriage match the narrated entrance.
Levitical priests rise to bless the gathered people, with the open sky suggesting prayer reaching heaven. Hezekiah is not inserted merely because he appears in the section cast.
The father reaches the returning son and embraces and kisses him, capturing the reunion described. Running momentum and the first embrace can share one instant.
An unnamed frightened man and a threatening military presence illustrate the verse's comparison of anguish to a king ready for battle. Neither Job nor Eliphaz is substituted for that described man.
Abundance reaches people and their storehouses through light and wind, matching Wisdom's promised provision. Wisdom receives no body, face, clothing or seat.
The Hatter's wide-eyed riddle and Alice's bright interest are the central interaction. The table's other guests remain present without literalizing the raven or writing-desk comparison.

The action explicitly sequences Alice examining the bottle and then drinking, rather than choosing one instant. The bottle label is requested without specifying visible words, so visible writing is not clearly demanded.

The plan selects the stone-gathering instant and includes the staff, five stones, pouch and sling. It additionally places Philistine ranks on the slope, whereas the verse identifies only the single Philistine David approaches.

The promised gift of living water to whoever thirsts becomes a spring appearing at John's own feet on a mountain. The listener is thereby made the visible recipient inside the scene described by the promise.

Lestrade's forehead-tapping gesture is assigned to Watson, and Holmes reaches for his coat before Lestrade has left rather than after the door closes. The table's clippings also request visible printed material.

Peter raises the man by his right hand as the man's feet strengthen, accurately preserving the healing action. John and the recurring crowd are additionally selected and depicted although this verse only places the healer and healed man in the scene.

The verse addresses a person claiming to guide the blind, but the plan makes its writer Paul the literal lamp-bearing guide. This changes both the referent and the rhetorical statement into an invented road encounter.

The burning house and three fire-engines match the approach described. The plan names the traveling group individually but leaves out Inspector Bradstreet, part of the party established by the adjacent exchange and 'we were all'.
The dietary description of the pig becomes a staged lesson by Moses and Aaron to families at camp. Those recurring teachers are selected despite not being present actors in the moment's description.
The arriving disciples see the charcoal fire with fish and bread, all of which appear in the plan. This verse does not require a visible Jesus beside the breakfast.

Samuel anoints David among his brothers, with wind suggesting the Spirit rather than a human form. Jesse is additionally selected and staged watching, though this verse specifies the brothers and Samuel, not the father.

Holmes throws the newspaper bundle toward the rack, but papers still spill across the seat and floor after the text says he rolled them all into the ball. The newspapers explicitly request visible printed material.

David's lowered sling arm and Goliath's face-first collapse correctly capture the strike's immediate aftermath. The recurring Philistine and Israelite armies are additionally staged watching, although this verse only describes the two combatants.

The Israelites cross dry ground between water walls on both sides, matching the verse. Moses is additionally selected and shown with his arm lowered after an earlier gesture, which the moment itself does not describe.
Holmes holds the blue stone to the light while Watson watches, matching the opening action. People mentioned in the gem's history and investigation are not inserted into the room.
The priest disposes of the crop and feathers beside the altar's eastern ash heap, matching the ritual instruction. The plan keeps the act restrained and does not add Moses as its performer.

Moses pours anointing oil onto Aaron's head, the action assigned to the addressed 'you' and 'him'. The commanded participants themselves are depicted, rather than the divine speaker taking bodily form.

The plan combines Holmes pulling Watson in and shutting the door with Wilson's half-rise of greeting. The text places Wilson's greeting after the subsequent exchange and introduction, not during the doorway action.
The rebel band fits the prophesied uprising and no visionary narrator is inserted. The king of the south, the explicit target, is reduced to distant banners rather than represented in the scene.

The clue is one paper with a note on one side and a hotel bill on the reverse, but secondaryElements describes a bill fragment and a pencilled note separately on the table while Holmes holds another paper. Both written surfaces also trigger visible_writing.
An unnamed runner sheds a weight before a watching crowd, illustrating the verse's race and witness imagery. Jesus or an identified author is not placed in that role.

The verse places the act after the Levite returns to his own house, but the setting explicitly locates it in Gibeah. The poised knife and covered body otherwise convey the grave act without lingering gore.

Moses extends his hand while wind parts the sea at night, with Yahweh represented through cloud and radiance. The plan additionally stages the Israelite people gathering on shore although the verse itself names only Moses and Yahweh as actors.
Alice questions the Dormouse at the tea table while the other guests remain in the conversation. The three sisters in the embedded story are not falsely added to the tea party.
The speaker is the one made to lie down and led to water, but the plan turns David into the shepherd settling a separate flock. That reverses his role in the words being illustrated.
